project.name: CodeCouncil
project.description: CodeCouncil is an independent, execution-grounded AI peer reviewer that watches a Claude Code session in real time, pairs the agent's stated intent with actual git changes, and only speaks after verifying a finding by running a repro. It writes claims-vs-verified session receipts and rewrites its own review heuristics from graded outcomes, with every rewrite gated by frozen evals and auto-rolled-back on measured regression. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: console.py
nodes.summary: Interactive slash-command console for the running council (/keys, /model, /prober, /status, /verbose, /config), applying changes in place and restarting the critic subprocess when needed. Pure command parsing is separated from side effects, and non-TTY stdin never starts a console.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberate purity split: parse_command is I/O-free and testable, while all mutation lives in the Console class the launcher owns.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker making core/ an importable Python package for the small shared utilities (store, redact, knowledge, config) that the four daemon loops are allowed to cross-import.

nodes.name: knowledge.py
nodes.summary: Repo-fact knowledge store shared between the Critic and Reflector loops: the Reflector distills one durable fact per rebutted finding into a capped, deduped .codecouncil/knowledge.md bullet list, and the Critic reads it on every judgment so the same rebuttal never recurs.
nodes.languageNotes: Lives in core/ rather than either loop because both need it and neither owns it; the on-disk file is swapped atomically via temp file + os.replace in the same directory.

nodes.name: redact.py
nodes.summary: Central credential redaction applied at observer capture time: pattern-matches API keys, OAuth tokens, PEM blocks, JWTs, credentialed URLs and secret-shaped assignments, replacing each with a «REDACTED:kind» marker so no raw credential ever reaches prompts, receipts, harvested eval cases, or the dashboard.
nodes.languageNotes: The «REDACTED:kind» marker is itself taught downstream as a confirmed secret-in-code finding, so redaction doubles as a signal rather than only suppressing data.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Module entry point letting the critic daemon run as `python3 -m critic`; delegates straight to critic.main.main with sys.argv.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Core of the Critic loop: the beat that reads new observations from a committed byte offset, mechanically screens the diff, dispatches judgment turns through a single-worker TurnScheduler, verifies findings by running a repro before delivery, merges primary and prober verdicts in council mode, and runs the end-of-task review that writes a session receipt.
nodes.languageNotes: Crash-safety is structural: the batch's read offset only commits after its verdict record lands, so a crash replays the batch rather than silently skipping it.

nodes.name: prompt.py
nodes.summary: Builds every prompt the Critic sends — judgment prompts (project header, numbered heuristics, distilled knowledge facts, verdict history, screening signals, new and touched file contents, budget-trimmed diff) and end-of-task review prompts — and parses the model's PASS/SUGGESTION reply with redaction and length caps.
nodes.languageNotes: Token budgeting reserves touched-file contents before the diff so the diff always keeps a guaranteed floor; the diff is the last thing trimmed.

nodes.name: render.py
nodes.summary: Terminal presentation layer for critic verdicts: loud colorized suggestion blocks, quiet PASS lines, a council-agreement gloss that flags uncorroborated prober-only findings, and an explicit warning when a model reply was malformed.

nodes.name: parse_command
nodes.summary: Pure, I/O-free parser turning a typed console line into a (command, argument) pair, returning None for anything that is not a slash command.

nodes.name: Console
nodes.summary: Side-effecting console handler owning /help, /verbose, /quit, /keys, /model, /prober, /status and /config; writes config, prompts for hidden key input, and restarts the critic subprocess so changes take effect without restarting the launcher.

nodes.name: build_distill_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the TASK: DISTILL prompt asking the model to extract exactly one durable repo fact from a rebutted finding plus the coding agent's rebuttal evidence.

nodes.name: parse_fact
nodes.summary: Validates a model-produced fact: enforces single-sentence length limits and rejects directive, imperative and suppressive shapes so injected instructions can never enter the knowledge file.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads the accumulated repo facts from .codecouncil/knowledge.md, returning empty text when the file is absent so callers never need to branch on existence.

nodes.name: add_fact
nodes.summary: Appends a validated fact with punctuation-insensitive deduplication and a 30-fact cap that evicts the oldest entry, rewriting the file atomically via temp file plus os.replace.

nodes.name: redact
nodes.summary: Applies every credential pattern to a text blob and replaces matches with «REDACTED:kind» markers; the single choke point every text-bearing field passes through at capture time.

nodes.name: load_state
nodes.summary: Loads the critic's persisted beat state (byte offsets, sticky test-run records), discarding and rebuilding it rather than crashing when the JSON fails to parse.

nodes.name: project_context
nodes.summary: Assembles the per-repo project header for prompts from capped CLAUDE.md and README excerpts, failing open and omitting the block when a file is unreadable.

nodes.name: verdict_history
nodes.summary: Joins recent suggestions with their reflector grades into a bounded verdict-history block so the judge sees which of its past calls were accepted or rebutted.

nodes.name: save_case_material
nodes.summary: Persists the events and diff behind a verdict as a judgment packet — PASS verdicts included — so any verdict can later be harvested and replayed as a frozen eval case.

nodes.name: normalize_file
nodes.summary: Maps staging-directory and absolute paths from verification runs back to repo-relative paths so every finding cites a real file in the watched repo.

nodes.name: reviewed_files
nodes.summary: Computes the set of files a verdict actually examined, recorded on every verdict so the reflector can later detect a PASS that missed a bug in one of them.

nodes.name: judge_batch
nodes.summary: Runs one judgment turn end to end: mechanically screens the diff, builds and sends the prompt (plus the optional prober call when verification is enabled), verifies any finding by running a repro, merges council verdicts, and returns the record to append.

nodes.name: probe_pass
nodes.summary: Opt-in property-probe pass: for a changed function carrying a docstring promise, spends one budgeted model turn deriving short self-checking scripts, executes them for real, and turns a caught code/docstring contradiction into a finding.

nodes.name: ask_with_retry
nodes.summary: Sends a prompt to the model and retries once when the reply is malformed, keeping the last reply so provider format drift degrades to a counted PASS instead of silently muting the critic.

nodes.name: resolve_prober
nodes.summary: Resolves the council prober model with flag-beats-env-beats-off precedence, so no council key is ever added to a suggestion unless a prober is explicitly configured.

nodes.name: merge_council
nodes.summary: Merges the primary and prober verdicts into one record with an agreement label, letting the primary's verdict flow through whenever it has one and marking prober-only findings as trusted only after a repro reproduces them.

nodes.name: should_task_review
nodes.summary: Debounce guard deciding whether a fresh 'done' declaration warrants another task review, given the cooldown window and the number of new requests.

nodes.name: recent_events
nodes.summary: Reads a bounded recency window of observations newer than a given epoch using the tail reader, so the unbounded observations log is never re-parsed whole.

nodes.name: sticky_tests_run
nodes.summary: Resolves the three-state 'did a test command actually run' fact from the sticky per-session record, honoring a max age so a genuine test run hours earlier still counts.

nodes.name: task_review
nodes.summary: Runs the review triggered when the coding agent declares work done: checks the claims against the diff and the mechanical test-integrity fact, then writes a claims-vs-verified session receipt.

nodes.name: TurnScheduler
nodes.summary: Single-worker scheduler for model turns: enforces a spacing gate between calls, queues and merges batches arriving while busy, re-queues a failing batch up to three times before dropping it loudly, and commits the read offset only after the record lands.

nodes.name: heartbeat
nodes.summary: One critic beat: reads new observations from the committed byte offset, gates on whether code actually changed, records sticky test runs, submits the batch to the scheduler, and triggers a task review when work is declared done.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the critic daemon: parses flags (--once, --judge-every-beat, --prober, --probes, --no-verify), assembles the run context and heuristics, and loops the heartbeat.

nodes.name: _diff_added_lines_per_md_file
nodes.summary: Counts added lines per markdown file across a diff, including untracked and touched-file material — the input to the plan-material heuristic.

nodes.name: is_plan_material
nodes.summary: Decides whether a change is substantially a plan or design-document edit, which switches the judgment prompt into plan-review mode via an addendum.

nodes.name: _render_touched_contents
nodes.summary: Renders the capped current contents of touched files into the prompt, budget-reserved ahead of the diff so the diff's minimum share still holds.

nodes.name: numbered_heuristics
nodes.summary: Renders heuristics.md bullets with stable R1./R2. indices so a suggestion can cite the exact rule that motivated it and the reflector can report acceptance per rule.

nodes.name: _render_knowledge
nodes.summary: Renders the distilled repo-facts section that follows the heuristics block in judgment and task-review prompts, omitted entirely when no facts exist.

nodes.name: build_prompt
nodes.summary: Assembles the full judgment prompt — project header, numbered heuristics, knowledge facts, verdict history, mechanical screening signals, new and touched file contents, and the diff — enforcing a token budget that trims the diff last.

nodes.name: tests_run
nodes.summary: Detects from observed tool calls whether a test command actually ran in the current batch of events.

nodes.name: mechanical_fact
nodes.summary: Produces the deterministic, non-model three-state 'did tests run' fact line embedded in task-review prompts and session receipts.

nodes.name: build_task_review
nodes.summary: Builds the end-of-task review prompt: the agent's claims, the diff and touched contents, numbered heuristics, knowledge facts, and the mechanical test-run fact the model must not contradict.

nodes.name: parse_reply
nodes.summary: Parses the model's reply into a PASS-with-reason or exactly one structured SUGGESTION, redacting and length-capping issue and rationale text and degrading malformed replies to a counted PASS.

nodes.name: _council_line
nodes.summary: Renders a short human-readable gloss for a verdict's council agreement outcome, explicitly calling out prober-only findings as not yet corroborated.

nodes.name: render_verdict
nodes.summary: Prints a verdict to the terminal — colorized suggestion block or quiet PASS, plus the council line and an explicit warning when the model reply was malformed.

nodes.name: test_core.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for core.store's bounded tail reader: small files return everything, large files return only the tail and drop the partial first line, a missing file is not fatal, and unparseable NDJSON lines are skipped rather than crashing.

nodes.name: test_critic.py
nodes.summary: Test suite for the Critic's pure logic: PASS/SUGGESTION reply parsing with redaction and length caps, judgment-prompt assembly and token budgeting, plan-material detection, fail-open project-context invariants, malformed-reply retry, screening-signal threading, and malformed-verdict visibility.

nodes.name: test_critic_beat.py
nodes.summary: Integration tests for the Critic beat loop and TurnScheduler driven by a stubbed model: change gating, committed-offset crash replay, batch re-queue and poison-batch drop, session tagging, sticky test-run records, reviewed-files bookkeeping, and prompt/case-material pruning caps.

nodes.name: test_critic_council.py
nodes.summary: Tests for council mode: merge_council's agreement matrix across every primary/prober outcome pair, prober-only findings surviving only after verification, the no-prober path staying byte-identical to pre-council behavior, and prober resolution from flag, env, or the local env file.

nodes.name: test_critic_receipts.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the end-of-task review and session receipt: test-command detection, the sticky three-state test-integrity fact, receipt sections (claims, files changed, findings joined with outcomes, dependencies), pruning to fifty, and end-to-end receipt writing including an unwritable receipts directory.

nodes.name: test_knowledge.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the shared knowledge store: single-sentence fact validation that rejects directive-injection and imperative shapes, punctuation-insensitive deduplication with a 30-fact eviction cap, and distill-prompt contents.

nodes.name: test_redact.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive redaction tests spanning AWS, NVIDIA, OpenAI, GitHub (classic, fine-grained, OAuth), Slack, Stripe, Google and Groq key shapes, PEM blocks, bare JWTs and credentialed URLs, plus negative cases (ordinary code, comments, plain URLs) that must stay untouched.

nodes.name: TestReadTailRows
nodes.summary: Covers read_tail_rows' bounded-read contract: full return for small files, tail-only with the partial first line dropped for large ones, missing-file tolerance, and skipping unparseable lines.

nodes.name: TestParseReply
nodes.summary: Exercises parse_reply across PASS variants, fenced and prose-wrapped JSON suggestions, missing keys, and malformed output degrading to PASS, plus redaction and the 300/600-char issue and rationale caps.

nodes.name: TestPrompt
nodes.summary: Verifies judgment-prompt assembly: section presence and ordering, project header first, heuristics numbering, knowledge placement, verdict history, commit events, event windowing, and the token budget that trims the diff last while touched contents stay capped.

nodes.name: TestPlanReview
nodes.summary: Tests is_plan_material's boundaries across tracked, untracked and touched markdown versus Python diffs, and that the plan-review addendum appears in the prompt only when the change is plan material.

nodes.name: TestProjectContextInvariants
nodes.summary: Pins project_context's fail-open behavior: no section without CLAUDE.md, excerpts capped with a truncation marker, and unreadable CLAUDE.md or README omitting the block instead of raising.

nodes.name: TestNormalizeFile
nodes.summary: Checks that staging-directory and absolute paths produced during verification map back to repo-relative paths.

nodes.name: TestAskWithRetry
nodes.summary: Confirms a malformed first reply is retried and recovered, and that a double failure keeps the last reply rather than raising.

nodes.name: TestScreenSignalThreading
nodes.summary: Verifies mechanical screening signals reach the verdict record: a security suggestion carries the matched screen signal and exploit addendum, while a non-security suggestion carries no screen-signal field.

nodes.name: TestMalformedVisibility
nodes.summary: Guards the invariant that provider format drift is never silent: a garbage stub reply produces a malformed-flagged record and a visible console warning, while a clean PASS produces none.

nodes.name: TestHeartbeatWithStub
nodes.summary: End-to-end beat tests with a stubbed model: no call without new events, reasoning-only batches gated and merged into the next diff batch, timestamps written post-verification, sticky per-session test-run recording and pruning, and verdict history read via a bounded tail.

nodes.name: TestReviewedFiles
nodes.summary: Asserts every verdict — including commit-only batches and PASS verdicts — records reviewed_files and saves case material, so silences remain gradeable and miss-detectable.

nodes.name: TestJudgeToolsPlumbing
nodes.summary: Pins the investigate-before-speaking contract: JUDGE_TOOLS stays read-only, judgment turns receive the path-jailed repo tools, and eval scoring stays tool-less for hermeticity.

nodes.name: TestSchedulerCooldown
nodes.summary: Verifies the TurnScheduler's spacing gate holds calls apart, that drain bypasses it, and that zero spacing dispatches back to back.

nodes.name: TestSchedulerAsync
nodes.summary: Checks that events arriving while the worker thread is busy are queued and merged into a single follow-up batch rather than dropped.

nodes.name: TestSchedulerRequeueOnFailure
nodes.summary: Confirms a failed batch is re-queued and replayed without advancing the committed offset, so a crash or model error never silently skips observations.

nodes.name: TestSchedulerPoisonBatchDrop
nodes.summary: Covers the bounded-retry escape hatch: a batch failing three times is dropped with a warning while the committed offset stays untouched, and the retry counter resets after a successful dispatch.

nodes.name: TestSessionTagging
nodes.summary: Verifies verdicts are tagged with the majority session of their events, sessionless batches tag none, and task reviews stay repo-wide with no session tag — the basis for session-scoped delivery.

nodes.name: TestCommittedOffset
nodes.summary: Pins the committed-offset crash-safety contract: a clean beat advances and round-trips it, a crash before append leaves it behind so the batch replays, legacy state without the key does not reset the offset, and sticky test-run records persist.

nodes.name: TestPromptAuditCap
nodes.summary: Checks the audit-trail growth bounds: saved prompts and case material prune beyond their cap, oversized case material is skipped, and saved packets round-trip their events and diff.

nodes.name: TestJudgeBatchCaseMaterial
nodes.summary: Confirms judge_batch writes case material for both SUGGESTION and PASS verdicts, so every judgment — including silences — is harvestable as an eval case.

nodes.name: TestMergeCouncil
nodes.summary: Exhaustive agreement matrix for merge_council across every primary/prober combination of suggest, pass and error, pinning which verdict wins and which agreement label is recorded.

nodes.name: TestCouncilJudgeBatch
nodes.summary: Integration tests for council mode inside judge_batch: prober-only findings survive with an agreement label, a prober agent error never blocks the primary verdict, no prober means one call and no council key, and --no-verify skips the prober entirely.

nodes.name: TestCouncilRenderRegression
nodes.summary: Regression tests that render_verdict prints the council line for both PASS-with-both-agreement and suggestion-with-prober-only-agreement verdicts.

nodes.name: TestResolveProber
nodes.summary: Pins resolve_prober's precedence: the flag beats the env var, the env var is used when no flag is given, and neither means council mode stays off.

nodes.name: TestMainResolvesProberFromLocalEnv
nodes.summary: Verifies a COUNCIL_PROBER entry in the out-of-repo local env file activates council mode through the daemon's main entry point.

nodes.name: TestTaskReview
nodes.summary: Covers test-command detection, task-review prompt content, the sticky middle and hard-no test-integrity states, and the should_task_review debounce.

nodes.name: TestReceiptContent
nodes.summary: Pins every section of the claims-vs-verified session receipt: claims pulled from commit subjects and claimy reasoning (capped at six and truncated), files changed from the diff stat, findings joined with outcomes and windowed, the three test-integrity states, the optional dependencies section, and pruning to fifty receipts.

nodes.name: TestReceiptTaskReviewIntegration
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests with a stubbed model that a task review writes a receipt reflecting weakened tests and new dependency lines, and that an unwritable receipts directory does not kill the review.

nodes.name: TestParseFact
nodes.summary: Validates parse_fact's facts-not-instructions filter: accepts a single sentence, rejects empty and over-long input, and rejects directive-injection, imperative and suppressive shapes.

nodes.name: TestAddFact
nodes.summary: Checks add_fact's deduplication ignoring trailing punctuation and the 30-fact cap that evicts the oldest entry.

nodes.name: TestBuildDistillPrompt
nodes.summary: Confirms the distill prompt carries the TASK marker, the rebutted finding, and the coding agent's rebuttal evidence.

nodes.name: TestRedact
nodes.summary: Single large table of redaction cases: every supported provider key shape, PEM blocks, JWTs and credentialed URLs are replaced, secret-shaped assignments keep the variable name while fully redacting the value, and ordinary code, comments and plain URLs stay untouched.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Package execution shim that makes `python3 -m codecouncil` work by delegating straight to the launcher's main().
nodes.languageNotes: Python `__main__.py` convention: the module executed when the package is run with -m.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: The CodeCouncil launcher: preflights the pi/model/prober setup, installs Claude Code hooks, then runs the observer, critic and reflector as subprocesses with signal-filtered prefixed output and an interactive console.
nodes.languageNotes: Subprocess fan-out with one daemon thread per child pumping stdout, plus SIGINT-then-kill shutdown — stdlib-only by project rule.

nodes.name: preflight
nodes.summary: Checks that the pi binary and the required API keys resolve (including an openrouter/* prober needing OPENROUTER_API_KEY) and returns human-readable warnings instead of letting the critic fail silently every beat.

nodes.name: _pump
nodes.summary: Per-daemon stdout reader thread: tags each line with the loop name and routes it through the signal filter so idle-beat chatter is dropped unless /verbose is on.

nodes.name: resolve_settings
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective model and prober settings from CLI flags, environment and the persisted config, in that precedence order.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses args (repo defaults to cwd), installs hooks, spawns observer/critic/reflector (and the UI dev server when node_modules exists), starts the interactive console on a TTY, then supervises and shuts the children down cleanly.

nodes.name: signal_filter.py
nodes.summary: Pure signal-vs-noise classification for the launcher's terminal: regex rules sort each daemon line into highlight (findings, verified proofs, grades, rewrites, receipts, council votes), normal narration, or dropped idle chatter.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately I/O-free so the classification is trivially unit-testable; ANSI escapes are stripped before matching.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Strips ANSI codes from a daemon output line and returns HIGHLIGHT, DROP or NORMAL by matching it against the highlight and idle-chatter patterns.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Shared persistence for CodeCouncil's per-repo JSON config and the out-of-repo ~/.codecouncil/env credential file, plus the flag > env > config resolution helper used by the launcher and console.
nodes.languageNotes: Both writers go through mkstemp + os.replace for atomicity; the env file is chmod-restricted since it holds API keys.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Reads the repo's JSON config file, returning an empty dict when it is missing, unparseable, or not a JSON object — never raising.

nodes.name: save_config
nodes.summary: Merges updates into the existing config (None values delete keys) and rewrites the file atomically via a temp file plus os.replace.

nodes.name: update_env_key
nodes.summary: Sets or removes a single KEY=value line in ~/.codecouncil/env, preserving other lines and comments, writing atomically and tightening file permissions afterwards.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Implements the project-wide setting precedence — explicit flag beats environment variable beats persisted config key.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: The shared NDJSON/JSON persistence layer every loop communicates through: tolerant row readers (whole-file and bounded tail), an append helper, atomic JSON writes, and a startup wait-for-file helper.
nodes.languageNotes: Readers deliberately skip unparseable and partial trailing lines because these files are appended to mid-write by other daemons.

nodes.name: read_rows
nodes.summary: Reads every parseable row of an NDJSON file, skipping malformed and partial trailing lines; used by completeness-critical consumers such as dedup sets and metric reports.

nodes.name: read_tail_rows
nodes.summary: Seeks to the last max_bytes of an NDJSON file, discards the truncated first line, and parses the remainder — the bounded-growth read used by hot paths and recency consumers.

nodes.name: append_row
nodes.summary: Appends one JSON-serialized row plus newline to an NDJSON log, creating parent directories as needed.

nodes.name: write_json_atomic
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON object through a temp file and os.replace so a crash mid-write can never leave a corrupt state or ledger file behind.

nodes.name: wait_for
nodes.summary: Polls until a required input file appears, printing a one-time waiting message — the reason daemons wait on missing inputs instead of dying.

nodes.name: receipt.py
nodes.summary: Renders the claims-vs-verified session receipt the critic writes when the coding agent declares work done, pairing the agent's stated claims with files changed, the tests-run fact, test-integrity screening and this session's verified findings.
nodes.languageNotes: The receipt embeds a machine-readable test-integrity JSON block that parse_test_integrity reads back, so the hooks layer can gate on it without re-running screening.

nodes.name: _test_integrity_line
nodes.summary: Turns a test-integrity screening result into a one-line human verdict (weakened / strengthened / unchanged) with the assertion and test counts that justify it.

nodes.name: parse_test_integrity
nodes.summary: Extracts the embedded machine-readable test-integrity JSON block back out of a written receipt, returning None when the block is absent or malformed.

nodes.name: _claims
nodes.summary: Mines the observation event stream for what the coding agent claimed it did — commit subjects plus reasoning text matching claim verbs — truncated for the receipt.

nodes.name: _findings
nodes.summary: Collects the suggestions raised inside this session's time window from suggestions.ndjsonl and joins each with its verification outcome and reflector grade.

nodes.name: write_receipt
nodes.summary: Assembles and writes the timestamped markdown session receipt into .codecouncil/receipts/ — verdict, claims, files changed, tests-run fact, test-integrity block, new dependencies and findings — then prunes the receipts directory.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker that makes hooks/ importable as a Python package by peer_hook, the tests and the eval harness.

nodes.name: install.py
nodes.summary: Idempotently installs CodeCouncil's PostToolUse / UserPromptSubmit / Stop hook entries into a watched repo's Claude Code settings, merging into any existing configuration without clobbering it.
nodes.languageNotes: Refuses to touch settings files that are malformed or not a JSON object rather than rewriting them — a deliberate do-no-harm bias.

nodes.name: merged_settings
nodes.summary: Pure merge of the peer_hook command into each hook event's matcher list, skipping events that already reference it and returning which ones were added.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Reads the repo's Claude Code settings, applies merged_settings, and writes the result atomically — bailing out untouched if the existing file is unparseable or not an object.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python3 -m hooks.install /path/to/repo`, validating the repo directory and reporting which hook events were newly wired.

nodes.name: ledger.py
nodes.summary: The delivery ledger persisted to delivered.json: records which suggestion ids went out on which channel, plus reserved keys tracking announced receipts, test-integrity Stop blocks, and sessions that already spent their one done-gate wait.
nodes.languageNotes: Reserved keys ("receipts", "test_integrity", "gate") are chosen to be invalid 12-char hex, so they can never collide with a real suggestion id.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads delivered.json and returns the TTL-pruned ledger, degrading to an empty ledger rather than raising when the file is missing or corrupt.

nodes.name: _pruned
nodes.summary: Drops ledger entries older than LEDGER_TTL_SECONDS and any malformed non-dict entries, keeping the reserved receipts/test-integrity/gate sub-maps intact so delivered.json cannot grow unbounded.

nodes.name: logic.py
nodes.summary: The pure, I/O-free decision core of the hooks layer: given a hook event, the current suggestions, the ledger and the receipts, it decides what to inject as context, whether to block a Stop declaration, and which receipt to announce.
nodes.languageNotes: Kept deliberately side-effect free so every delivery, session-scoping, TTL, council-verification and done-gate rule is exhaustively unit-testable.

nodes.name: gate_pending
nodes.summary: Reports whether the critic still has unjudged material worth waiting for — true only when a tail event is a diff or commit, never for reasoning-only chatter.

nodes.name: resolve_gate_seconds
nodes.summary: Resolves the opt-in done-gate wait budget from COUNCIL_GATE_SECONDS or the config key, clamping to GATE_SECONDS_MAX and treating unset, zero, negative and malformed values as off.

nodes.name: _session_ok
nodes.summary: Enforces session-scoped delivery: a session-tagged suggestion only reaches the session whose work produced it, while untagged repo-wide rows always pass.

nodes.name: _pending
nodes.summary: Selects the suggestions eligible for a given channel — right severity, within TTL, not already delivered, session-matched, and (for prober-only council findings) verified by a repro.

nodes.name: _describe
nodes.summary: Renders one suggestion row into the human-readable finding text injected into the coding agent's context, including the invitation to reply with COUNCIL-REBUTTAL.

nodes.name: _pick_receipt
nodes.summary: Chooses the newest session receipt that has not yet been announced through the ledger's reserved receipts key, so each receipt is announced exactly once.

nodes.name: _test_integrity_block
nodes.summary: Decides whether the newest receipt's "weakened" test-integrity verdict should block this Stop, allowing exactly one block per receipt via the reserved test_integrity ledger key.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: The single decision entry point: dispatches on hook event type to produce injected context, a receipt announcement, or a Stop block — dropping the block-severity floor from high-only to medium+ when the done-gate actually held this turn.

nodes.name: peer_hook.py
nodes.summary: The executable Claude Code hook: reads the hook event on stdin, gathers suggestions/ledger/receipts, optionally holds a Stop open while the critic catches up, then emits the pure logic layer's decision — always failing open to a silent exit 0.
nodes.languageNotes: The delivered.json read→decide→write span is flock-guarded (itself fail-open), and the done-gate poll happens outside that lock so a sleep never holds it.

nodes.name: _locked
nodes.summary: Context manager taking a real exclusive flock around the ledger read-decide-write span, and silently proceeding unlocked if the lock path is unusable so the hook never dies on locking.

nodes.name: _read_critic_state
nodes.summary: Reads the critic's persisted state to learn its committed observation offset, treating a missing or malformed state file as caught up.

nodes.name: _read_unjudged_events
nodes.summary: Reads the observation rows past the critic's committed offset — the material the critic has seen but not yet judged — used to decide whether the done-gate should wait.

nodes.name: _maybe_wait_for_critic
nodes.summary: The opt-in done-gate: when unjudged diff/commit material exists at Stop, polls (outside any lock, clamped to the max budget, once per session) so a finding landing in that window can still be delivered this turn.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Orchestrates one hook invocation: parses the event, loads suggestions, ledger and receipts, runs the pure decide() under the flock, persists the ledger, and returns the hook JSON response.

nodes.name: _list_receipts
nodes.summary: Lists the session receipt files newest-first so the decision layer can pick the most recent unannounced one.

nodes.name: _attach_test_integrity
nodes.summary: Parses each receipt's embedded test-integrity block onto the receipt record, skipping receipts that fail to decode so a malformed file never raises.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point wrapping run() so that any error at all results in a silent exit 0 — the hook's fail-open invariant.

nodes.name: test_hooks.py
nodes.summary: The exhaustive stdlib-unittest suite for the hooks layer: fail-open behaviour, ledger locking and pruning, every delivery/blocking/session-scoping rule in logic.decide, council prober-only verification, receipt announcement, the done-gate, and hook installation.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes pure-function tests of logic.decide with real subprocess end-to-end runs of peer_hook.py, so the fail-open and locking invariants are checked in a real process, not just in-process.

nodes.name: suggestion
nodes.summary: Test factory building a suggestion row with configurable id, severity, timestamp, file/line, session tag, council block and verification result.

nodes.name: TestFailOpen
nodes.summary: Asserts the hook's fail-open invariant against garbage stdin and a missing .codecouncil directory, plus end-to-end subprocess runs covering injection, receipt announcement and a test-integrity Stop block.

nodes.name: TestPeerHookLocking
nodes.summary: Proves _locked takes a real exclusive OS lock, fails open on an unusable lock path, wraps the whole load-decide-save span, and makes two interleaved hook processes deliver exactly once.

nodes.name: TestLedgerPruning
nodes.summary: Checks TTL pruning drops old entries while keeping fresh ones and the reserved sub-maps, and that malformed non-dict entries are dropped rather than raising.

nodes.name: TestDecideContext
nodes.summary: Covers PostToolUse context injection: medium/high delivered but low ignored, delivered-once semantics, TTL expiry, PASS/id-less rows skipped, the three-finding cap and malformed-row tolerance.

nodes.name: TestDecideSessionStart
nodes.summary: Verifies UserPromptSubmit delivers findings and shares the same ledger channel as PostToolUse so nothing is announced twice.

nodes.name: TestDecideStop
nodes.summary: Pins the ungated Stop rules: high severity blocks exactly once, medium never blocks, stop_hook_active always allows through, and context delivery does not consume the block.

nodes.name: TestDecideStopGated
nodes.summary: Covers the lowered block floor when the done-gate actually held: medium blocks once only in the gated case, while stop_hook_active and high-severity behaviour stay unchanged.

nodes.name: TestSessionScopedDelivery
nodes.summary: Checks on both the context and block channels that a session-tagged finding reaches only its own session while untagged repo-wide rows always deliver.

nodes.name: TestCouncilProberOnlyGate
nodes.summary: Enforces that a prober-only council finding is delivered only when verification reproduced it — inconclusive or verification-less rows stay silent — while agreement cases and no-council rows behave exactly as before.

nodes.name: TestReceiptAnnouncement
nodes.summary: Verifies a session receipt is announced once on PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit, appended to existing findings text, never announced on Stop, and that decide stays free of filesystem access.

nodes.name: TestDoneGateTestIntegrity
nodes.summary: Covers the weakened-test-integrity Stop gate: it blocks exactly once per receipt, ignores unchanged/strengthened/key-less receipts, respects stop_hook_active, yields to a high-severity block, and only ever considers the newest receipt.

nodes.name: TestAttachTestIntegrityMalformed
nodes.summary: Checks that a receipt with malformed UTF-8 is skipped without a test-integrity key and without raising.

nodes.name: TestGatePending
nodes.summary: Pins gate_pending's contract: diff and commit events are pending, reasoning-only or empty tails are not, and events missing a type key are ignored.

nodes.name: TestResolveGateSeconds
nodes.summary: Covers gate-budget resolution: off by default, env beats config, zero/negative/malformed values are off, and both sources are clamped to the maximum.

nodes.name: TestDoneGateWait
nodes.summary: The done-gate wait loop under test: off by default so it never sleeps, delivers a finding that lands mid-wait, runs at most once per session, fails open on unreadable critic state, and never holds the ledger lock across a sleep.

nodes.name: TestInstall
nodes.summary: Verifies hook installation is idempotent on a fresh repo, preserves unrelated existing settings, and leaves malformed or non-object settings files untouched instead of crashing.

nodes.name: test_store.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the shared store's atomic JSON writer: valid round-tripping, parent-directory creation, and that an interrupted write leaves the original file intact.

nodes.name: TestWriteJsonAtomic
nodes.summary: Exercises write_json_atomic end to end, proving the crash-safety invariant that a failure mid-write cannot corrupt the pre-existing file.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker that makes `critic` an importable Python package so its modules (agent, screen, deps, probe, verify) can be imported as `critic.*` by the daemons and the test suite.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: The single model boundary for all of CodeCouncil: runs one non-interactive, session-less pi agent turn (`pi -p --no-session`) with the persona supplied via --system-prompt, and resolves the model/credentials (COUNCIL_MODEL, PI_BIN, NVIDIA_API_KEY) from the real environment topped up by the never-committed ~/.codecouncil/env file.
nodes.languageNotes: Stdlib-only subprocess wrapper; CRITIC_CMD swaps the executable for a deterministic stub in tests, and the bundled NVIDIA provider extension is always attached via `pi -e`.

nodes.name: deps.py
nodes.summary: Zero-model-cost dependency-provenance screen: flags typo-suspect imports one edit away from a well-known package name (the slopsquatting shape, where the wrong package still resolves) and extracts newly added dependency-manifest lines from a diff.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure and offline by design; the local `from . import screen` inside new_dependency_lines breaks a deliberate import cycle between the two screening modules.

nodes.name: pkg_names.py
nodes.summary: Curated offline snapshot of roughly 400 well-known PyPI packages' top-level import names, used as the reference set for deps.py's one-edit typo-suspect check.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately precision-over-coverage and all-lowercase: mixed-case import names (PIL, Cython, PyQt5) are excluded because a lowercase typo could never match them.

nodes.name: probe.py
nodes.summary: Property probes — the 'almost-right' detector. Reconstructs changed functions that carry a docstring promise straight from the diff's added lines, spends one budgeted model turn deriving short self-checking scripts, and executes them for real in a throwaway staging copy; a probe that demonstrates code contradicting its own docstring becomes a finding whose repro is the probe itself.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `ast` to reconstruct added functions from `+` lines only, so candidate extraction stays pure and testable without a repo on disk; execution is isolated via a scrubbed env and a HOME redirected into the staging dir.

nodes.name: screen.py
nodes.summary: Mechanical screening of a diff's added lines for the documented top AI-code failure modes — injection patterns, unsafe deserialization, weakened tests, and unresolvable or typo-suspect imports — producing attention signals the judgment prompt asks the model to confirm or dismiss.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure except `resolve_new_imports`, which spawns one python in the watched repo; eval replays pass no repo so screening stays hermetic.

nodes.name: AgentError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a pi agent turn fails to run or returns an unusable result; callers such as verify_finding catch it to degrade to an 'error' status instead of crashing the critic beat.

nodes.name: local_env
nodes.summary: Reads ~/.codecouncil/env (a credentials file deliberately kept outside any watched repo) and returns its key/value pairs, letting the real process environment win over file entries.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Runs one ephemeral, non-interactive pi turn with the given prompt and persona, resolving model/executable/env and optionally attaching path-jailed read-only tools; returns the model's stdout reply or raises AgentError.

nodes.name: _within_one_edit
nodes.summary: Bounded edit-distance predicate: true when two names differ by exactly one substitution, insertion, deletion, or adjacent transposition — the distance metric the slopsquat check is built on.

nodes.name: is_typo_suspect
nodes.summary: Decides whether an import name is a one-edit typo of a well-known package name (and not itself a real name), i.e. the resolvable-but-wrong slopsquatting shape.

nodes.name: suspicious_imports
nodes.summary: Maps newly imported top-level names to screening signals for those that look like typos of well-known packages, naming the intended package as evidence.

nodes.name: new_dependency_lines
nodes.summary: Extracts added dependency declarations from a diff by recognizing manifest files (requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, package.json) and returning their new entries for provenance review.

nodes.name: _added_blocks
nodes.summary: Groups a diff's contiguous runs of added lines per Python file into standalone text blocks that can be parsed independently of the file on disk.

nodes.name: _parse_block
nodes.summary: Attempts to parse an added-lines block into a Python AST, dedenting as needed, so a fragment lifted out of a class or nested scope still yields a tree.

nodes.name: _walk_functions
nodes.summary: Walks an AST collecting function definitions with their qualified names, so methods added to an existing class are still identifiable.

nodes.name: candidates
nodes.summary: Diff-only, filesystem-free extraction of changed functions that carry a docstring promise — the deliberately conservative pure half of the probe pass, deduped and testable without a repo.

nodes.name: build_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the budgeted model prompt asking for short self-checking probe scripts derived from a candidate function's docstring promise, capping the embedded source with an explicit truncation marker.

nodes.name: strip_fence
nodes.summary: Strips markdown code fences from a model reply so a fenced script still executes; shared with critic/verify.py.

nodes.name: run_script
nodes.summary: Shared execution primitive: writes a script into a staging directory and runs it under sys.executable with a scrubbed environment and a HOME redirected into staging, bounded by a timeout.

nodes.name: _execute_probe
nodes.summary: Runs one derived probe script against the staged copy of the changed file and classifies whether it demonstrated a contradiction, agreed with the docstring, or simply errored.

nodes.name: _line_for
nodes.summary: Resolves the source line number of a qualified function name inside a file so a probe finding can point at real coordinates.

nodes.name: run_probes
nodes.summary: End-to-end probe pass for one candidate: copies the file into a throwaway staging dir, spends one model turn to derive probes, executes them in order, and returns the first demonstrated docstring contradiction as a finding carrying its own repro.

nodes.name: added_lines_by_file
nodes.summary: Parses a unified diff into per-file lists of (line number, text) for added lines — the substrate every mechanical check operates on.

nodes.name: removed_lines_by_file
nodes.summary: Parses a unified diff into per-file lists of removed line texts, used by the test-weakening and test-integrity checks.

nodes.name: scan_patterns
nodes.summary: Scans added lines for injection-shaped strings, shell/eval usage, and unsafe deserialization, emitting CWE-tagged signals with the offending line as evidence.

nodes.name: scan_test_weakening
nodes.summary: Flags diffs that delete test functions or strip assertions without replacement — the agent-under-pressure failure mode of weakening the tests instead of the code.

nodes.name: test_integrity
nodes.summary: Classifies a diff's net effect on test strength (strengthened / unchanged / weakened) from added-vs-removed test functions and assertion counts, backing the session receipt's test-integrity line.

nodes.name: new_import_names
nodes.summary: Extracts newly imported top-level module names (and the file each came from) from a diff's added Python lines.

nodes.name: resolve_new_imports
nodes.summary: The one impure check: spawns a single python inside the watched repo to ask which newly imported top-level modules actually resolve there, flagging the ones that do not as hallucinated imports.

nodes.name: screen
nodes.summary: Runs every mechanical check over a diff and returns the capped signal list; repo=None (eval replay) skips the import-resolution subprocess, and typo-suspect runs before unresolvable-import so each imported name yields exactly one signal.

nodes.name: match_signal
nodes.summary: Precision-first matcher linking a model suggestion back to the mechanical signal that motivated it, requiring the same file basename plus the CWE kind named in the issue — proximity alone never attaches, and ambiguous multi-signal cases attach nothing.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the signal list into the compact section injected into the judgment prompt, framed as attention direction the model must confirm or dismiss.

nodes.name: verify.py
nodes.summary: The prove-it-before-speaking step: stages the flagged file into a throwaway directory, asks a no-tools model turn for ONE self-contained repro script, and has the harness (never the model) execute it — verified findings ship with a repro, refuted ones are never delivered.
nodes.languageNotes: Replaced an earlier tool-enabled turn because the pi/NVIDIA backend emitted tool calls as literal, never-executed text; a harness-executed script has no such failure mode.

nodes.name: test_agent.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the model boundary: credential file layering (~/.codecouncil/env vs real env), default-model resolution, pi command-line construction for tool/cwd modes, and the exact argv a CRITIC_CMD stub receives.

nodes.name: test_deps.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the dependency-provenance screen: one-edit distance semantics, typo-suspect flagging, dependency-manifest line extraction, and the ordering contract between the typo-suspect and unresolvable-import checks in screen().

nodes.name: test_probe.py
nodes.summary: Unit and integration tests for property probes: diff-only candidate extraction, prompt capping, divergent-vs-consistent probe outcomes, and the critic-main wiring covering budget caps, opt-in defaults, cross-beat dedup, redaction, and staging-environment scrubbing.

nodes.name: test_screen.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for mechanical screening: security-pattern detection, test-weakening and test-integrity classification, hallucinated-import handling, signal-to-suggestion matching precision, and byte-identical prompt rendering when no signals exist.

nodes.name: test_verify.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for finding verification: prompt contract, CWE exploit addenda, script-execution outcomes (confirmed/refuted/inconclusive/timeout/crash), repro localization, and the delivery policy that refuted findings never reach the developer.

nodes.name: build_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the no-tools verification prompt asking for ONE self-contained repro script against the staged file, appending a CWE-specific exploit addendum when the linked screening signal has a known template.

nodes.name: localize_repro
nodes.summary: Rewrites absolute staging-directory paths in a repro script to a relative './' form so the repro the developer receives is runnable in their own repo.

nodes.name: _classify
nodes.summary: Turns a repro script's stdout/stderr/exit code into verified, refuted, or inconclusive — both markers present, no marker, or an unexpected crash all fall back to inconclusive rather than a false verdict.

nodes.name: verify_finding
nodes.summary: Verifies one finding end to end: stages the flagged file in a throwaway dir, asks the model for a repro script, executes it via the shared run_script primitive, and returns the status plus a redacted, capped, path-localized repro when verified.

nodes.name: TestLocalEnv
nodes.summary: Covers the ~/.codecouncil/env credential-file layering: file values fill unset vars, the real environment always wins, a missing file is non-fatal, and the NVIDIA default model is chosen only when COUNCIL_MODEL is unset and a key is present.

nodes.name: TestAskCommandConstruction
nodes.summary: Asserts the exact pi command line ask() builds — read-only tool flags with a cwd, an explicit model parameter overriding COUNCIL_MODEL, and falling back to env resolution when no model is passed.

nodes.name: TestAskStubModelArgv
nodes.summary: Pins the CRITIC_CMD stub contract: the resolved model is always passed as the second argv, including the empty-string case when nothing resolves.

nodes.name: TestWithinOneEdit
nodes.summary: Exercises the one-edit distance predicate across substitution, deletion, insertion, adjacent transposition, and the negative cases of two edits or a length delta of two.

nodes.name: TestSuspiciousImports
nodes.summary: Verifies typo-suspect flagging names the intended package, never flags the real name or a stdlib name, ignores far-off unknowns, and evaluates each imported name independently.

nodes.name: TestIsTypoSuspect
nodes.summary: Direct unit coverage of the is_typo_suspect predicate for known, typo'd, and unrelated names.

nodes.name: TestNewDependencyLines
nodes.summary: Confirms new dependency entries are extracted from requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, and package.json diffs while unrelated files and empty diffs yield nothing.

nodes.name: TestSocketerRegression
nodes.summary: Regression guard for a stdlib-adjacent name that must not be typo-flagged yet must still be caught as an unresolvable import when a repo is available.

nodes.name: TestScreenOrdering
nodes.summary: Locks the screen() ordering contract: a typo-suspect name is excluded from the unresolvable-import check so each imported name produces exactly one signal, with and without a repo.

nodes.name: TestCandidates
nodes.summary: Covers diff-only candidate extraction: only added functions carrying a docstring qualify, non-Python files and partial edits are skipped, methods fall back to a bare name, and duplicates are deduped.

nodes.name: TestBuildPromptCap
nodes.summary: Asserts oversized source is truncated with an explicit marker in the probe prompt while small source passes through untouched.

nodes.name: TestRunProbes
nodes.summary: End-to-end probe execution tests: a diverging probe produces a finding with a repro, consistent or raising probes produce none, fenced replies still parse, and model errors or missing files fail closed without a finding.

nodes.name: TestCriticMainWiring
nodes.summary: Integration tests for probes inside the critic beat: the model-call budget caps candidates, probes stay off by default, a diverging probe becomes its own suggestion row, secret-shaped notes are redacted, results dedupe across beats, and a transient error does not permanently suppress a candidate.

nodes.name: TestRunScriptEnvScrub
nodes.summary: Proves the shared execution primitive scrubs the environment, redirects HOME into the staging directory, and runs under sys.executable.

nodes.name: TestResolveProbes
nodes.summary: Covers the opt-in resolution order for probes: flag beats env, env enables when no flag is given, and the default is off.

nodes.name: TestSecurityPatterns
nodes.summary: Asserts the injection/deserialization pattern scanner flags f-string SQL, shell=True, os.system, unsafe yaml and pickle, and eval on a variable — while parameterized SQL, safe loaders, literal_eval, and comments stay clean.

nodes.name: TestTestWeakening
nodes.summary: Covers detection of removed test functions and stripped assertions, and confirms an assertion refactor or a non-test file is not flagged.

nodes.name: TestTestIntegrity
nodes.summary: Pins the three-state test-integrity classification (strengthened / unchanged / weakened) across added assertions, new test functions, equal-count refactors, removed tests, and net-negative assertion changes.

nodes.name: TestHallucinatedImports
nodes.summary: Verifies new import names are parsed from added Python lines only and that unresolvable imports are flagged while stdlib names are not.

nodes.name: TestMatchSignal
nodes.summary: The precision contract for signal-to-suggestion matching: basename plus named CWE attaches, proximity alone never does, reward-hacking signals never attach, and ambiguous or unrelated cases attach nothing.

nodes.name: TestScreenAndPrompt
nodes.summary: Confirms screening stays hermetic without a repo, respects the signal cap, and leaves the judgment prompt byte-identical when there are no signals.

nodes.name: TestBuildPrompt
nodes.summary: Asserts the verification prompt carries the finding and path, requests CONFIRMED/REFUTED markers, and asks for a script rather than tool calls.

nodes.name: TestVerifyFindingBasics
nodes.summary: Confirms a finding pointing at a missing file resolves to inconclusive without spending any model call.

nodes.name: TestExploitAddenda
nodes.summary: Covers CWE exploit addenda: known CWEs append a short addendum, unknown ones and a None signal leave the prompt byte-identical, and verify_finding threads the screening signal all the way into the prompt the model sees.

nodes.name: TestScriptVerification
nodes.summary: The core verification matrix: confirmed scripts yield a repro, refuted scripts are refuted, and raising, timing-out, empty, marker-less, both-marker, or post-marker-crash replies all degrade to inconclusive rather than a false verdict.

nodes.name: TestVerifyFindingReproIsExecutedScript
nodes.summary: Proves the delivered repro is the actual executed script text with staging paths localized to the developer's repo.

nodes.name: TestLocalizeRepro
nodes.summary: Unit coverage of staging-prefix rewriting, including the no-prefix passthrough case.

nodes.name: TestDeliveryPolicy
nodes.summary: Locks the delivery policy: refuted findings never reach the developer, verified ones ship with proof and a verify-it-yourself hint on both the injection and block channels, and inconclusive or unverified findings still deliver.

nodes.name: TestPromptContract
nodes.summary: Guards the prompt contract that an unexpected error must never be reported as REFUTED.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: Frozen-case evaluation harness: replays a fixed set of observation payloads through every archived heuristics version using real critic model calls, then prints a catches/clean-passes score table.
nodes.languageNotes: Inserts the repo root onto sys.path before importing critic/observer so the module works as both a CLI (python3 -m evals.run) and a lazily-imported library used by the rewrite gate.

nodes.name: load_cases
nodes.summary: Loads every frozen eval case: hand-made cases from evals/cases first, then auto-harvested ones from evals/cases-harvested so curated cases always sort first.

nodes.name: heuristics_versions
nodes.summary: Collects every heuristics version available in a watched repo — archived heuristics-history/v*.md files plus the live heuristics.md — deduped by version and sorted.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Scores one case against one verdict: a 'pass' case requires a PASS verdict, a 'flag' case requires a SUGGESTION naming one of the case's expected files.

nodes.name: score_heuristics
nodes.summary: Runs one real model call per frozen case against a given heuristics text and returns the fraction correct — the controlled comparison the rewrite gate and the CLI report both build on.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: scores every heuristics version of a repo against the frozen cases, appends each per-case result to .codecouncil/evals.ndjsonl, and prints the improvement table.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the reflector loop, the daemon that grades delivered suggestions and rewrites the critic's heuristics.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Module entry point so `python3 -m reflector /path/to/repo` runs the reflector daemon's main() and exits with its status code.

nodes.name: harvest.py
nodes.summary: Turns graded outcomes into frozen eval cases under the shared, gitignored evals/cases-harvested directory, so the case set that gates heuristics rewrites grows from real in-the-wild signal.
nodes.languageNotes: HARVESTED_DIR is a module-level Path (not a function) specifically so tests can monkeypatch it, and it is deliberately global across every watched repo — cross-repo learning is the design intent, not an accident.

nodes.name: _write_case
nodes.summary: Shared dedupe/cap/write tail for both harvest paths: skips a case whose content hash already exists, writes the frozen case JSON, then prunes the directory to the newest 40 by mtime.

nodes.name: maybe_harvest
nodes.summary: Decides whether a graded outcome qualifies as a new eval case: accepted+verified becomes a must-flag case, refuted or untouched-file rebuttals become must-pass, and a missed PASS becomes a must-flag case keyed on (file, fix-commit subject).

nodes.name: judge.py
nodes.summary: Pure grading helpers for the reflector: which delivered suggestions are ripe to grade, what post-delivery evidence to bundle, the TASK: GRADE prompt, and a strict reply parser.

nodes.name: first_delivery
nodes.summary: Returns the earliest delivery timestamp across all hook channels for a suggestion id, or None if it was never delivered.

nodes.name: pending
nodes.summary: Splits ungraded SUGGESTION rows into those ripe for a model-judged grade (delivered long enough ago for the agent to react) and those never delivered, which grade 'undelivered' for free.

nodes.name: evidence
nodes.summary: Bundles everything observed in the window after delivery — agent reasoning, tool calls, commits, the latest diff, and new/untracked file contents — into the evidence block of the grading prompt.
nodes.languageNotes: Untracked and touched file contents are rendered verbatim because a real fix can live entirely in a new file that never shows up in a tracked diff; they are already redacted and capped at observer capture time.

nodes.name: explicit_rebuttal
nodes.summary: Deterministic rebuttal detector: finds the COUNCIL-REBUTTAL marker the hook invites in post-delivery reasoning and returns the stated reason, skipping the model call entirely.

nodes.name: file_touched
nodes.summary: Model-free cross-check signal: did the flagged file appear in any post-delivery diff, commit, or untracked-file listing within the evidence window.

nodes.name: build_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the TASK: GRADE prompt asking the model to classify the delivered suggestion as accepted, rebutted, or ignored with one sentence of evidence, in a strict JSON shape.

nodes.name: parse_grade
nodes.summary: Strictly parses the grading reply, tolerating code fences and the 'grade' key alias models drift to; anything malformed degrades to 'ignored' with the raw reply retained for inspection.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Reflector daemon: on a slow heartbeat it grades delivered suggestions and missed PASSes into outcomes.ndjsonl, distills rebuttal facts, harvests eval cases, then rolls back or rewrites heuristics.md behind the eval gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Every best-effort side path (distillation, harvesting, miss detection) is wrapped in a blind except so the daemon never dies on an unexpected error — intentional fail-open code, not a defect.

nodes.name: grade_pending
nodes.summary: One grading pass: marks never-delivered suggestions 'undelivered', grades delivered ones via the explicit rebuttal marker or a model call, distills a repo fact from rebuttals, harvests eval cases, and deterministically grades missed PASSes.

nodes.name: maybe_rewrite
nodes.summary: Generates a heuristics rewrite candidate once enough fresh grades accumulate, applying it only after both strict format validation and the frozen-eval gate pass — and advancing the grade counter on either rejection so a stale candidate is not regenerated every pass.

nodes.name: maybe_rollback
nodes.summary: Auto-reverts the current heuristics version when its in-the-wild acceptance drops below its predecessor's, restoring the old rules as a new higher version number and guarding against repeat rollbacks.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI/daemon loop: waits for the critic's suggestions file, then repeatedly grades, rolls back, rewrites, and atomically persists reflector state until --once or interrupt.

nodes.name: report.py
nodes.summary: Renders the improvement curve as tables: acceptance rate per heuristics version plus per-rule and per-failure-mode breakdowns, with a deterministic file_touched cross-check column.
nodes.languageNotes: 'missed' outcomes are counted but deliberately kept out of the acceptance denominator so the two measurement signals (in-the-wild acceptance vs frozen evals) stay independent.

nodes.name: consistent
nodes.summary: Cross-checks a model grade against the deterministic file_touched signal, returning None when the comparison does not apply (rebuttals are consistent either way).

nodes.name: build_rows
nodes.summary: Aggregates suggestions and outcomes into one row per heuristics version — suggested/delivered counts, each grade, acceptance rate, cross-check rate, and the inconsistent rows to warn about.

nodes.name: build_rule_rows
nodes.summary: Per (version, cited heuristic rule) counts — the surgical companion to build_rows that answers 'did R3 specifically do well', with cite-less findings kept visible in a rule=None bucket.

nodes.name: build_mode_rows
nodes.summary: Per (version, failure_mode) counts, answering where the critic's decorrelated checks actually land versus where they are just noise; untagged findings land in a None bucket.

nodes.name: render_rule_rows
nodes.summary: Formats per-rule aggregation rows into a fixed-width table, labelling the rule=None bucket 'R?'.

nodes.name: render_mode_rows
nodes.summary: Formats per-failure-mode aggregation rows into a fixed-width table, labelling the untagged bucket '?'.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Formats the main per-version table and appends warning lines for grades that disagree with the deterministic file_touched signal.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: reads suggestions and outcomes for a repo and prints the version table, plus the per-rule and per-mode tables when that attribution data exists.

nodes.name: rewrite.py
nodes.summary: Heuristics rewrite machinery: rule parsing, the evidence-linked rewrite prompt, strict format validation, the frozen-eval gate that blocks regressions, and the archive-then-atomic-swap apply.
nodes.languageNotes: Both the evals.run and .report imports are deliberately lazy (inside functions) to keep the module import graph acyclic across the reflector loop.

nodes.name: rules
nodes.summary: Parses heuristics.md into a list of top-level bullet rules with continuation lines joined onto their parent.

nodes.name: rewrite_record
nodes.summary: Builds the ledger entry describing what a rewrite changed — rules added and removed, grade counts that drove it, and a one-line headline.

nodes.name: should_rewrite
nodes.summary: Gate on volume: a rewrite is attempted only when enough newly graded outcomes have accumulated since the last one, or when forced.

nodes.name: _rule_stat_lines
nodes.summary: Per-rule stat lines for the current heuristics version only, derived from report.build_rule_rows so the rewrite prompt can argue 'R3: 0/2 accepted, drop it'.

nodes.name: _mode_stat_lines
nodes.summary: Per-failure-mode stat lines for the current version, derived from report.build_mode_rows, answering whether a decorrelated check ever lands.

nodes.name: build_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the TASK: REWRITE HEURISTICS prompt: the current file, every graded outcome, aggregate stats, and per-rule and per-mode breakdowns, with the exact output contract for version N+1.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Strict format check on a rewrite candidate — non-empty, unfenced, exact 'version: N+1' first line, and within the 40-line cap — returning an error string or None.

nodes.name: gate_candidate
nodes.summary: The eval gate: scores the candidate and the current heuristics on the same frozen cases and passes only when the candidate does not regress; with no cases at all it passes through ungated.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Archives the outgoing heuristics version to heuristics-history/vN.md, then atomically swaps the new text into place via a temp file and os.replace.

nodes.name: harvest_isolation.py
nodes.summary: Shared unittest base class that redirects reflector.harvest's global HARVESTED_DIR to a per-test temp directory, so no test ever writes into the repo's real harvested-cases directory.

nodes.name: HarvestIsolatedTestCase
nodes.summary: TestCase base that monkeypatches the harvest module's HARVESTED_DIR (and the evals runner's harvested-cases path) to a temp directory for the duration of each test.

nodes.name: test_evals.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the frozen-case evaluation runner: score computation from stubbed PASS/SUGGESTION verdicts, the empty-case-set edge case, and well-formedness of the shipped cases' failure-mode slices.

nodes.name: TestScoreHeuristics
nodes.summary: Verifies score_heuristics computes the correct fraction from stubbed model replies and returns zero rather than crashing on an empty case list.

nodes.name: test_harvest.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for eval-case harvesting: which grade/verification combinations produce flag, pass, or no case; redaction survival; content-hash dedupe including the missed-PASS commit-subject key; and the directory cap.

nodes.name: TestMaybeHarvest
nodes.summary: Exhaustive table of maybe_harvest behaviours across accepted/rebutted/ignored/missed outcomes, verification statuses, dedupe keys, and the 40-case eviction cap.

nodes.name: test_reflector.py
nodes.summary: The reflector loop's main test suite: grading eligibility and evidence bundling, grade parsing, rewrite guardrails and the eval gate, auto-rollback, knowledge distillation, outcome attribution fields, and missed-PASS grading.
nodes.languageNotes: Model calls are stubbed through CRITIC_CMD, with stubs branching on prompt-content markers such as 'TASK: REWRITE' to answer several prompt kinds from one script.

nodes.name: TestGradePendingBoundedReads
nodes.summary: Asserts the read-boundedness contract: suggestions/observations use the bounded tail reader while the graded-ids dedup set reads the whole outcomes file.

nodes.name: TestPending
nodes.summary: Covers judge.pending eligibility: delivered-and-mature is judged, recently delivered waits, never delivered times out to 'undelivered', already graded is skipped.

nodes.name: TestEvidence
nodes.summary: Covers evidence bundling: the post-delivery window filter, inclusion of untracked and touched file contents, and the cap on the new-file section.

nodes.name: TestParseGrade
nodes.summary: Covers grade parsing: valid JSON, fenced output, the 'grade' key alias, and malformed replies degrading to 'ignored'.

nodes.name: TestRewriteGuardrails
nodes.summary: Covers the rewrite threshold and force flag, validation rejections, per-rule and per-mode stats appearing in the prompt, the rewrite ledger record, and archive-then-swap on apply.

nodes.name: TestReport
nodes.summary: Covers acceptance math per version, cross-check consistency rules, the explicit rebuttal marker, and the exclusion of undelivered and missed outcomes from acceptance.

nodes.name: TestGateCandidate
nodes.summary: Covers the frozen-eval gate: a lower-scoring candidate fails, an equal score passes, and no cases directory means ungated pass-through.

nodes.name: TestMaybeRewriteGateIntegration
nodes.summary: End-to-end gate integration: a gate failure leaves heuristics.md untouched, a pass applies and records the gate note, and a failure backs off so the next pass makes no model calls on unchanged outcomes.

nodes.name: TestMaybeRollback
nodes.summary: Covers auto-rollback: it reverts once then no-ops, advances state so the following rewrite does not thrash, honours the revert-once guard, and treats a missing archive as a no-op.

nodes.name: TestGradePendingHarvestsCases
nodes.summary: Covers harvesting from grade_pending: accepted grades harvest a flag case, explicit rebuttals with an untouched file harvest a pass case, and a harvest failure never kills the grading pass.

nodes.name: TestGradePendingCreditsUntrackedFix
nodes.summary: Regression test that a fix living entirely in a new untracked file is graded accepted rather than under-credited as ignored.

nodes.name: TestGradePendingDistillsKnowledge
nodes.summary: Covers fact distillation on both rebuttal paths (explicit marker and model-judged) and that a distillation failure never kills grading.

nodes.name: TestOutcomeRowsCarryRule
nodes.summary: Asserts rule attribution is copied onto outcome rows on both grading paths and is absent on undelivered rows.

nodes.name: TestOutcomeRowsCarryCouncilAgreement
nodes.summary: Asserts council agreement is copied onto outcome rows when a prober was configured, is null otherwise, and is absent on undelivered rows.

nodes.name: TestMissedGrading
nodes.summary: Covers deterministic missed-PASS grading: it grades and harvests, is idempotent across passes, survives detection failure, and carries no council-agreement field.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker that makes `observer/` an importable Python package so the daemon can run as `python3 -m observer`.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Module entry shim that delegates `python3 -m observer` to observer.main.main().
nodes.languageNotes: Python's `__main__.py` convention lets a package be executed directly with `-m`.

nodes.name: events.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Observer's wire format: the `Event` dataclass (beat, type, payload, session, ts) and `EventLog`, the append-only NDJSON writer that every loop downstream reads.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a frozen-style dataclass plus `asdict()` for one-line JSON serialization — the only contract between the four daemons.

nodes.name: gitwatch.py
nodes.summary: Snapshots the watched repo's git reality into `diff` and `commit` event payloads: working-tree diff, untracked file contents, capped contents of touched files, and commit subjects/diffs over an old..new HEAD range. Every text-bearing field is passed through core.redact.redact() at capture time.
nodes.languageNotes: Shells out to `git` via subprocess with stdlib only; `fingerprint()` sha256-hashes the snapshot so a diff event is emitted only on real change.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: The Observer daemon's event-driven beat loop: locates the Claude Code project transcript directory, then on each beat pairs transcript intent (reasoning/tool_call) with git reality (diff/commit) and appends everything to observations.ndjsonl.
nodes.languageNotes: Beats fire when a transcript file grows (`transcript_sig` + `wait_for_material`); `--interval` is only a fallback floor, not a poll period.

nodes.name: render.py
nodes.summary: Terminal pretty-printer for one Observer beat, colorizing reasoning, tool calls, diff stats and commits into a compact human-readable line block.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: Persistent Observer state: per-transcript byte offsets, last diff fingerprint, last HEAD, beat counter and interval, loaded tolerantly and saved atomically so a crash mid-write can never corrupt it.
nodes.languageNotes: A parse failure discards and rebuilds state rather than raising — the daemon-never-dies invariant.

nodes.name: transcript.py
nodes.summary: Tails Claude Code session transcript JSONL from ~/.claude/projects/<munged-path>/ into `reasoning` and `tool_call` events, resolving the right project directory by cwd and reading only new bytes from a persisted offset. Reasoning text and tool-call commands are redacted at capture.
nodes.languageNotes: Byte-offset tailing keeps the hot path O(new bytes); a partial trailing line is deliberately left unconsumed until the next beat completes it.

nodes.name: misses.py
nodes.summary: Grades the Critic's silences: detects a fix-shaped commit that revises files a recent PASS verdict reviewed and deterministically marks that PASS as `missed`, requiring both a fix-subject match and an exact-path/basename overlap so precision comes first.
nodes.languageNotes: `missed` is kept out of the acceptance rate on purpose — two-signal separation between eval scores and in-the-wild acceptance.

nodes.name: test_gitwatch.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for observer.gitwatch covering untracked and touched file capture, per-file caps, binary/excluded-directory skipping, commit capture, fingerprint stability, and the redaction invariant across diffs, untracked contents and commit subjects.
nodes.languageNotes: Each test builds a real throwaway git repo in a TemporaryDirectory rather than mocking subprocess.

nodes.name: test_misses.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for reflector.misses: fix-subject regex variants, lookback windows, already-graded suppression, and the path-overlap matcher's guarantee that substring and cross-directory basename collisions never produce a false `missed` grade.

nodes.name: test_observer.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the Observer's transcript parsing, incremental byte-offset tailing with partial/truncated files, state round-tripping, NDJSON event-log validity, and the event-driven pacing helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Backed by a synthetic transcript fixture (tests/fixtures/session.jsonl); redaction assertions confirm secrets never reach parsed events.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing one observation: beat number, event type, payload dict, originating session id and ISO timestamp.

nodes.name: EventLog
nodes.summary: Append-only NDJSON writer that creates its parent directory on construction and serializes each Event as one JSON line to observations.ndjsonl.

nodes.name: _git
nodes.summary: Runs a git subcommand in the watched repo and returns its stdout, swallowing failures so a non-repo or broken git never kills the daemon.

nodes.name: _read_untracked
nodes.summary: Reads the contents of new untracked files, skipping binaries and excluded directories, redacting the text and capping each file's size with an explicit truncation marker.

nodes.name: _touched_paths
nodes.summary: Parses a unified diff's +++ headers to recover the list of files the working tree actually touched, excluding deletions.

nodes.name: _read_touched
nodes.summary: Reads capped, redacted current contents of every diff-touched tracked file so the Critic sees the file as it stands, not just the hunk.

nodes.name: capture
nodes.summary: Builds one working-tree snapshot: diff, diff --stat, untracked file list plus their contents, and touched-file contents — all redacted at capture time.

nodes.name: head
nodes.summary: Returns the repo's current HEAD sha, or None before the first commit exists.

nodes.name: capture_commits
nodes.summary: Captures the commit subjects and combined diff for an old..new HEAD range, redacting both before they become a commit event payload.

nodes.name: fingerprint
nodes.summary: sha256-hashes a snapshot's diff, untracked list and both content maps so a diff event is emitted only when the repo state genuinely changed.

nodes.name: heartbeat
nodes.summary: One Observer beat: collects new transcript events, emits a commit event when HEAD moved, and emits a diff event when the working-tree fingerprint changed, appending all of it to the event log.

nodes.name: transcript_sig
nodes.summary: Computes a cheap signature (paths plus sizes/mtimes) of the session transcript directory used to detect that new agent activity landed.

nodes.name: wait_for_material
nodes.summary: Blocks until the transcript signature changes or max_wait elapses — the event-driven pacing that makes --interval only a fallback floor.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses args, waits for the Claude Code project directory to appear, loads or rebuilds state, and runs the beat loop (once, from-start, or continuously) rendering each beat.

nodes.name: render_beat
nodes.summary: Prints one beat's events as a compact colorized block: reasoning excerpts, tool calls with salient inputs, diff stats and commit subjects.

nodes.name: State
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the Observer's persisted cursor — per-transcript byte offsets, last diff hash, last HEAD, beat counter and interval — with a tolerant `load` and an atomic `save`.

nodes.name: munge_path
nodes.summary: Converts a repo path into the dash-munged directory name Claude Code uses under ~/.claude/projects/.

nodes.name: _dir_matches_cwd
nodes.summary: Confirms a candidate project directory really belongs to this repo by inspecting the cwd recorded inside its session JSONL lines.

nodes.name: find_project_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the Claude Code session directory for a repo, first by munged-name guess and then by scanning all project directories for a cwd match.

nodes.name: tail_new_lines
nodes.summary: Reads only the bytes appended since the stored offset, returning complete lines and leaving a partial trailing line unconsumed; detects truncation and re-reads from zero.

nodes.name: _salient_tool_input
nodes.summary: Distills a tool call's input to the fields worth logging (command, file path, pattern), redacted and truncated.

nodes.name: parse_line
nodes.summary: Parses one transcript JSONL line into zero or more reasoning/tool_call Events, skipping non-assistant and sidechain entries and redacting every text-bearing field at capture.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Tails every session JSONL in the project directory from its persisted offset and returns the parsed events plus the updated offsets.

nodes.name: _paths_match
